extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures. MMMU focuses on advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.publisher: IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, common university majors are reviewed to decide which subjects should be included based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. Subjects like law and linguistics were ruled out due to difficulty finding relevant multimodal problems. In the second stage, over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. To mitigate data contamination, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers. This process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks spanning six common disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. Collected from major textbooks and online resources by 50+ university students across 30 subjects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. The second stage involved distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format. In the third and final stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations follow a detailed protocol where data must be accurate, consistent, and adhere to high academic rigor. Questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and not be ambiguous. Questions are categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended. All fields are annotated including question, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation. Data is stored in JSON format with standardized naming conventions. A secondary review team vets annotations for quality and guideline adherence, with regular audits of random samples. Ambiguities are flagged for collaborative review in team meetings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Three-stage quality control: (1) lexical overlap and source URL similarity to identify duplicates reviewed by authors; (2) format and typo checking distributed among co-authors; (3) categorization into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard) with ~10% of very easy problems excluded.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students (including co-authors) from various disciplines and subjects, specializing in the 30 target majors. For human expert evaluation: 90 college senior students selected to represent experts in 30 subjects (3 student experts per subject).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is actively maintained with a live-updating leaderboard available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard. Version change log is maintained (v1 Nov 2023 through v4 June 2024) with documented updates including addition of new model results.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information, in compliance with privacy laws and ethical standards.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to monitor progress toward Expert AGI, which marks a critical milestone where AI systems reach 'at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' in a broad range of tasks. This starts to achieve 'the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor' for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. It is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. Strong performance on MMMU is necessary but not sufficient for Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is divided into a few-shot development set (5 questions per subject, 150 total), a validation set (~900 questions) useful for hyperparameter selection, and a test set (10,500 questions). MMMU is designed to measure three essential skills in LMMs: perception, knowledge, and reasoning. Used to evaluate how well models can perceive and understand information across different modalities and apply reasoning with subject-specific knowledge.
